data.title: SpiceJet faces over 7,600 passenger complaints amid widespread flight cancellations
data.description:
The Centre has received over 7,000 complaints against beleaguered SpiceJet on its passenger complaints redressal portal, AirSewa, amid continued flight cancellations as well as passenger inconvenience.

According to the Ministry of Civil Aviation’s grievance page, 7,674 grievances were listed against the airline in data dated November 19.

SpiceJet cancellations raise winter travel concerns

Sources said most of the airline’s scheduled flights were cancelled on Friday, and its services did not appear in booking results on most online travel portals. The airline is currently operating around 10 aircraft, comprising aircraft from its own fleet and wet-leased planes.

These disruptions come ahead of the peak winter travel period, raising concerns about passenger inconvenience, alternative flight availability, and replacement fares.

However, the wider impact on domestic passenger traffic and fares is likely to be limited, given that SpiceJet’s market share stood at only 0.6 per cent in September, down from 1.2 per cent in August, according to Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) data.

Nevertheless, passengers booked on cancelled services could face higher last-minute fares, particularly on routes with limited alternatives.

The impact on fares would depend on seat availability on competing airlines on the affected routes during the winter travel period.

DGCA flags repeated regulatory violations

Meanwhile, the DGCA has issued a show-cause notice dated November 17, giving SpiceJet seven days to respond to alleged regulatory and operational non-compliance.

The notice flagged several repeated regulatory violations.

Furthermore, the regulator observed that a majority of SpiceJet’s fleet remained grounded and that the airline had failed to submit a credible plan to bring these aircraft back into service.

SpiceJet seeks ₹5,500 crore to revive operations

The regulatory scrutiny comes as the cash-strapped airline seeks fresh funding to strengthen its financial position, rebuild capacity and support its revival.

On Wednesday, SpiceJet’s board approved a proposal to raise ₹5,500 crore, subject to the necessary shareholder and regulatory approvals.

The airline has been struggling to pay employee salaries for several months amid a cash crunch.

Moreover, the budget carrier faces legal hurdles, including insolvency petitions filed by lessors and payment claims involving former promoter Kalanithi Maran and KAL Airways.

data.title: India Cements to initiate recovery of ₹26 crore arbitration award from Zuari, after SC dismisses SLP
data.description:
India Cements Ltd informed exchanges that the Supreme Court on Wednesday dismissed a Special Leave Petition (SLP) filed by Zuari Cement against India Cements in a dispute arising from a 2002 marketing agreement.

This has now cleared the way for India Cements to initiate recovery proceedings for ₹26.40 crore along with applicable interest, the company said.

As per the filing, the dispute relates to an Agreement in May 2002 between India Cements and Sri Vishnu Cement (which was subsequently merged with Zuari Cement).

While the Arbitral Tribunal had passed an award in favour of India Cements, directing Sri Vishnu Cement to pay ₹26.40 crore along with applicable interest, Zuari Cement had then challenged the award before the Madras High Court, where Zuari obtained a favourable judgement for itself.

India Cements then appealed to the High Court and managed to get it set aside, following which Zuari had filed an SLP before the Supreme Court.

“The company shall now initiate appropriate proceedings for recovery of the awarded amount, together with applicable interest, from Zuari Cements,” India Cements said in the filing.

Shares of India Cements were trading at ₹324.50, up 1 per cent on the BSE, at the time of filing the report.

data.title: Fincantieri wins Carnival contract for two next-generation cruise ships
data.description:
Italian shipbuilder Fincantieri said on Friday it had signed a contract with Carnival Corporation to build two next-generation dual-fuel cruise ships for Carnival Cruise Line, in a deal worth more than €2 billion ($2.20 billion).

  • The vessels, to be built at Fincantieri's Marghera shipyard and delivered in 2033 and 2035, will each have a gross tonnage of about 130,000 tons and around 1,650 guest cabins

  • The ships will be powered primarily by liquefied natural gas (LNG), Fincantieri said, adding the design could be used across multiple Carnival brands in the future

  • The two companies have been partners for 30 years during which Fincantieri has delivered 76 ships for Carnival, including 15 for Carnival Cruise Line

data.title: Max Healthcare, Apollo Hospitals shares rally up to 5% as Macquarie double upgrades
data.description:
Shares of Max Healthcare and Apollo Hospitals were in focus on Friday after global brokerage Macquarie double-upgraded both stocks to ‘outperform’, citing improving earnings prospects and cooling valuations.

Max Healthcare surged nearly 5 per cent in early trade to ₹1,090 on the NSE, leading the Nifty 50 gainers, while Apollo Hospitals gained 4 per cent to hit a fresh 52-week high of ₹9,097.

Macquarie double upgraded Max Healthcare and Apollo Hospitals to ‘outperform’, stating that consensus earnings have bottomed out and valuations have cooled off.

The brokerage believes that the initial profitability drag from the bed expansion cycle is already embedded in the stock prices, while new capacity is ramping up at a healthy pace.

Macquarie raised its target price for Max Healthcare to ₹1,450 and Apollo Hospitals to ₹10,500. The brokerage said Max Healthcare offers a better risk-reward proposition compared with Apollo Hospitals.

data.title: WMT Stock Ticks Higher Overnight: Analyst Says Walmart Deserves Rich Valuation, CEO Stands By ‘Low Price’ Game
data.description:
Key points:
  • Truist raised Walmart’s price target to $134 from $114 and maintained a Buy rating.
  • Truist sees Walmart’s advertising, marketplace and membership businesses supporting a premium stock valuation. 
  • Walmart CEO John Furner highlighted its low-price strategy as a driver of growth. 

Walmart Inc. (WMT) stock edged higher overnight as Truist raised its price target, saying the retailer deserves a premium valuation. CEO John Furner reaffirmed Walmart’s everyday low-price strategy on the third-quarter earnings call, citing market-share gains, strong customer and holiday demand.

Walmart stock edged nearly 1% higher overnight, ahead of Friday. However, the stock is on track to snap a six-week winning streak.

Truist Raises Walmart's Price Target After Q3 Results 

Truist lifted its price target for Walmart to $134 from $114 while maintaining a ‘Buy’ rating, implying a 6% upside from the stock’s last close. Analyst Scot Ciccarelli believes Walmart's operating performance strengthened in Q3 compared with the preceding three-month period.

According to the analyst, Walmart’s ability to offer competitive prices, combined with investments that make deliveries and order fulfillment faster, could help the retailer attract more shoppers and take business away from competitors.

Beyond traditional retail sales, Truist said Walmart is developing businesses that could contribute more to its earnings. Its advertising operations, third-party online marketplace and membership offerings provide additional sources of income, thus improving profits. Truist believes Walmart deserves a higher valuation than many other retailers because of its competitive advantages.

Low Prices Remain Central To Walmart's Strategy

During Q3 earnings call, Walmart CEO John Furner said the retailer continues to attract shoppers, with customer purchases and transaction activity showing strength. He also expressed confidence about the upcoming holiday shopping period.

“We’ve spent years investing in our people-led, tech-powered omnichannel approach so we can better serve customers and members. That starts with our everyday low price philosophy and our commitment to invest in price,” said Furner.

He credited the company's investments in employees, technology and its interconnected shopping channels for helping it serve customers across physical stores, warehouse clubs and online platforms.

The retailer's digital business continued to expand during the quarter. Worldwide e-commerce revenue increased 17%. In the U.S., online sales climbed 23% at Walmart and 30% at Sam's Club. Walmart now sees 2027 net sales to grow 4.9% to 5.2%, up from its earlier estimate of 4% to 5%.

WMT Stock: Retail View 

Retail sentiment around the stock improved to ‘bullish’ from ‘neutral’.

A user said, “$WMT another solid report. No question, a stock to always hold and sleep well at night. Because folks are always in Walmart.”

WMT stock has gained 13% year-to-date.

data.title: Union Pacific, Norfolk Southern Say Looking Forward To STB's Continued Evaluation Of Proposed Merger
data.description:
NORFOLK (dpa-AFX) - Union Pacific Corporation (UNP) and Norfolk Southern Corporation (NSC) have filed a response opposing Canadian Pacific Kansas City's request to end the Surface Transportation Board's (STB) review of their proposed merger, which would create the first single-line transcontinental railroad in the U.S.

The companies said they support a full, transparent and rigorous review of the proposed merger and encouraged all stakeholders to share their views with the STB.

CPKC had sought to end the review, alleging that Union Pacific CEO Jim Vena's remarks at a conference in March threatened commercial retaliation against those opposing the merger and discouraged shippers from participating in the review. Five shipper groups had also raised concerns about the remarks.

In an accompanying statement Vena said, 'I do use humor in my presentations to keep the audience engaged, including in my presentation at the conference of the Southwest Association of Rail Shippers this past March. I know what I said and regret the inference. The speech was over 50 minutes long, and I made an attempt at humor at the end of that presentation. I apologize to anyone who misunderstood my statement.'

Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern said the proposed deal would give U.S. businesses more options to 'compete globally, reduce transportation costs and protect tens of thousands of union jobs.'

The companies said they look forward to the STB's continued review of the proposed combination based on the facts, evidence and public interest benefits presented in the regulatory record.

On the NYSE, Union Pacific shares rose 0.47% in after-hours trading after closing at $290.63 on Thursday. Norfolk Southern shares, meanwhile, fell 2.06% to close at $316.82.

data.title: Retailer Mr Price's NKD deal boosts sales, but higher finance costs weigh on profit
data.description:
By Nqobile Dludla

South African retailer Mr Price reported on Friday a 2.2% rise in half-year earnings, with higher finance costs related to its acquisition of German discount retailer NKD Group weighing on growth.

  • The value-focused fashion and homeware retailer said diluted headline earnings per share (DHEPS), a key earnings figure, rose to 508.6 cents in the 26-week period ended September 26

  • Group retail sales rose 41.8% year-on-year to 25.3 billion rand ($1.44 billion), while operating profit increased 30.7% to 2.8 billion rand, helped by the contribution from its new European business

  • Finance costs jumped 145% to 1 billion rand as the group also refinanced NKD's German debt

  • Africa retail sales grew 3.1% to 18.4 billion rand, supported by 101 new stores, while comparable-store sales were flat as higher household spending on utilities and fuel weighed on disposable income

  • Africa gross profit margin increased 60 basis points to 40.6%, despite elevated promotional activity by competitors during the period

  • NKD contributed retail sales of 6.9 billion rand and operating profit of 526 million rand, outperforming the broader German apparel and value-retail markets, the company said

  • The group declared an interim dividend of 329.5 cents per share

($1 = 17.5532 rand)

data.title: FRO – Third Quarter and Nine Months 2026 Results
data.description:
FRONTLINE PLC REPORTS RESULTS FOR THE THIRD QUARTER ENDED SEPTEMBER 30, 2026

Frontline plc (the “Company”, “Frontline”, “we,” “us,” or “our”), today reported unaudited results for the nine months ended September 30, 2026:

Highlights

  • Profit of $641.4 million, or $2.88 per share for the third quarter of 2026 and adjusted profit1 of $530.9 million for the third quarter of 2026, or $2.38 per share.
  • Declared a cash dividend of $2.38 per share for the third quarter of 2026.
  • Reported revenues of $921.3 million for the third quarter of 2026.
  • Achieved average daily spot time charter equivalent earnings ("TCEs")2 for VLCCs, Suezmax tankers and LR2/Aframax tankers in the third quarter of 2026 of $148,500, $102,500 and $67,800 per day, respectively.
  • Sold two VLCCs built in 2017 for a total sales price of $270.0 million. The transactions generated net cash proceeds of $179.0 million, which were returned to the shareholders through the payment of a special one-time dividend of $0.80 per share in September 2026.
  • Entered into a three-year time charter-out agreement for one Suezmax tanker, built in 2016, at a rate of $80,000 per day, which commenced in October 2026.
  • Entered into a new senior secured revolving reducing credit facility in an amount of up to $731.8 million in November 2026 to refinance the $1,286.0 million secured revolving reducing credit facility, further reducing the Company’s weighted average interest rate margin to 118 bps as of the date of this report.

Lars H. Barstad, Chief Executive Officer of Frontline Management AS, commented:

“The third quarter of 2026 was defined by the escalation in the Middle East, logistical challenges and time-consuming trading patterns. Utilization has since reached extraordinary levels, and freight rates have moved to all-time highs, with asset values following and the entire tanker complex benefiting. As we are well into the fourth quarter of the year, our bookings so far are at the highest levels we have ever recorded across all three of our segments. With the majority of our spot days already fixed, Frontline is positioned to deliver its strongest result ever, both for the fourth quarter and for the full year 2026. The nine months that have passed in 2026 is likely to change the oil trading patterns considerably in the future, making us optimistic for Frontline’s earnings capacity in the years to come.”

Inger M. Klemp, Chief Financial Officer of Frontline Management AS, added:

“From June to November 2026 we reduced our financing costs through a combination of margin reductions on existing facilities for their remaining tenors and full refinancing of selected facilities, contributing to a reduction in the Company’s weighted average interest rate margin of 60 bps from 178 bps at the end of the first quarter of 2026 to 118 bps as of the date of this report.

We believe that the refinancing of, and amendments to, our existing debt facilities have been achieved on highly attractive terms, further strengthening our liquidity position while reducing our borrowing costs and cash breakeven rates. We continue to focus on maintaining our competitive cost structure, breakeven levels and solid balance sheet to ensure that we are well positioned to generate significant cash flow and create value for our shareholders.”

  • compliance with the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act of 1977 or other applicable regulations relating to bribery;
  • general economic conditions and conditions in the oil industry;
  • effects of new products and new technology in our industry, including the potential for technological innovation to reduce the value of our vessels and charter income derived therefrom;
  • new environmental regulations and restrictions, whether at a global level stipulated by the International Maritime Organization, and/or imposed by regional or national authorities such as the European Union or individual countries;
  • vessel breakdowns and instances of off-hire;
  • cost and effects of cybersecurity incidents or other failures, interruptions, or security breaches of our systems or those of our customers or third-party providers, including software failures, unforeseeable security breaches, or incidents stemming from the ability to successfully adopt artificial intelligence and digital logistics in our business;
  • our ability to successfully adopt artificial intelligence and digital logistics into our operating systems;
  • risks associated with potential cybersecurity or other privacy threats and data security breaches;
  • potential conflicts of interest involving members of our Board of Directors and senior management;
  • the failure of counter parties to fully perform their contracts with us;
  • changes in credit risk with respect to our counterparties on contracts;
  • our dependence on key personnel and our ability to attract, retain and motivate key employees;
  • adequacy and cost of insurance coverage;
  • our ability to obtain indemnities from customers;
  • changes in laws, treaties or regulations;
  • the volatility of the price of our ordinary shares;
  • our incorporation under the laws of Cyprus and the different rights to relief that may be available compared to other countries, including the United States;
  • changes in governmental rules and regulations or actions taken by regulatory authorities;
  • government requisition of our vessels during a period of war or emergency;
  • potential liability from pending or future litigation and potential costs due to environmental damage and vessel collisions;
  • the arrest of our vessels by maritime claimants;
  • general domestic and international political conditions or events, including “trade wars”;
  • any further changes in U.S. trade policy that could trigger retaliatory actions by the affected countries;
  • disruptions to global trade routes, including actual or threatened attacks on commercial shipping, military conflicts, piracy, terrorism, sanctions enforcement actions, restricted transit through strategic waterways, or other security incidents affecting the Strait of Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb, Red Sea, Suez Canal, Panama Canal or other major shipping routes;
  • the impact of increasing trade restrictions, tariffs, port charges, sanctions, export controls, and other protectionist measures; that may affect global oil trade flows, vessel utilization, customer demand, or operating costs;
  • changes in sanctions regimes, enforcement priorities or restrictions affecting oil transportation, vesseloperations or counterparties;
  • the impact of port or canal congestion; 
  • business disruptions due to adverse weather, natural disasters or other disasters outside our control; and
  • other important factors described from time to time in the reports filed by the Company with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

data.title: Honda Unveils All-new Avancier SUV With Next-generation Hybrid System
data.description:
TOKYO (dpa-AFX) - Honda Motor Co., Ltd. (HMC, 7267.T) on Friday unveiled its all-new Avancier SUV at an online world premiere, featuring its next-generation Honda Hybrid system and a newly developed platform, amid growing global demand for hybrid vehicles.

The Japanese automaker plans to roll out the new Avancier primarily in Asian markets, including Thailand, Japan and China.

Further, the company plans to launch 15 next-generation hybrid models globally by the end of the fiscal year ending March 31, 2030, starting with the new Avancier.

The Avancier is a three-row SUV designed for comfortable long-distance journeys.

It is the first Honda hybrid model to feature the company's new H mark and next-generation hybrid technology, which aims to deliver improved fuel efficiency and driving performance.

The vehicle also features a DualPower electric all-wheel-drive system, Motion Management System, Honda S+ Shift and over-the-air software updates.

In Tokyo, the shares were trading 2.35 percent lower at ¥1,748.00.

data.title: Novartis Stock Reaction to New Targets Seems Overdone — Market Talk
data.description: The market reaction to Novartis's medium-term targets seems overdone, with sales guidance as expected and executives pointing to AI gains that look set to boost profitability, RBC Capital Markets analysts say in a research note. "The +5% mid-term sales growth was in line with our expectations, and hopes for higher were unrealistic, in our view," the analysts say. Moreover, executives at the Swiss drugmaker did a good job explaining the prospects for growth drivers such as its key approved medicines Rhapsido and Kisqali, as well as drug candidates ianalumab and abelacimab, the analysts add. Novartis also detailed how AI is set to help it reduce costs and accelerate workflows, which could allow it to hit its 2029 profitability goal early, according to RBC. Novartis shares closed 3.2% lower at 127.24 Swiss francs. (adria.calatayud@wsj.com)
